# Joseph and Aseneth Chapter 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS | **Section:** Aseneth Rises on the Eighth Day

---

**1** On the eighth morning — still dark, before the rooster had crowed — Aseneth got up from her bed. She had no tears left.

**2** She said to herself: 'What do I do? There's nowhere to run, no one to help me. My father has promised me to Pharaoh's son. Joseph despises me for worshiping those dead idols.'

**3** 'I'll go to my father's God — Joseph's God. I'll call out to him. He is the Father of the orphaned, the champion of the helpless, the helper of the crushed.'

**4** Aseneth got up, went to the east window, and looked out. The sun was just coming up, the morning star still bright in the sky.

**5** She prayed: 'Lord, God of eternity — you made everything, you breathed life into it all, you brought the invisible into the light, you ordered everything into existence — I call out to you like a little child with no parents, a child taken captive by a stranger.'

**6** 'My own parents have rejected me because I smashed their idols. You are my only hope, Lord. Your mercy is my only refuge.'

**7** Aseneth stood up, set aside the fine linen clothes, and dressed in mourning — an old, faded black garment, tied with sackcloth.

**8** She pulled the golden crown from her head, the golden bracelets from her wrists, the anklets from her feet, and threw them all to the floor.

**9** She dumped ash on her head, dropped to the floor, beat her chest, and wept.

**10** She prayed to Joseph's God: 'Lord God of eternity — you give life, you call the living into being, you call people from darkness to light, from falsehood to truth, from death to life. Lord, you alone are gracious, merciful, patient, and gentle — more than any human or any so-called god.'

**11** 'Lord, I run to you. I bring you my prayer. I cry out to you. I confess my sins and the sins of my family before you.'

**12** 'Have mercy on me, Lord. I have sinned enormously. I am a godless woman who served dead, speechless idols. Lord, have mercy — I am alone and broken.'

---
*PNEUMA: modern English; verse-only numbering.*
